fix: Hoist `next` into a reusable buffer on `self.input` (for example `self.input.hover_scratch: Vec<ElementId>`): take it with `std::mem::take`, `clear()` it, refill it, and return it. The focus-behavior ids from `focus_behavior_elements` (line 614, also a fresh Vec) should be pushed into the same buffer instead of being returned as a new Vec.

Move `next` into the map instead of cloning it: `let previous = self.input.mouse_hover.insert(key, next).unwrap_or_default();`. Afterwards read the current set back with `self.input.mouse_hover.get(&key)` (or keep the scratch-buffer swap from the previous finding) so no per-event Vec clone happens.

Replace the per-event `previous_live`, `exits` and `enters` Vecs (lines 624-637) with reusable scratch buffers stored on `self.input` (cleared at the start of each pointer event). Compute `exits` and `enters` into those buffers, so the later passes iterate the buffers and no new allocation happens per move event.

The four snapshot Vecs (`exit_callbacks`, `enter_callbacks`, `enter_behaviors`, `exit_behaviors`, lines 638-662) and `hover_callbacks` (lines 676-682) are per-event allocations. Keep the snapshot semantics (callbacks run after all lookups) but store the snapshots in reusable scratch buffers on `self.input` (for example `Vec<Rc<dyn Fn(RawPointerEvent)>>` and `Vec<Rc<FocusBehavior>>`), cleared per event. Do not switch to lazy iterators: a callback may change the tree before later entries are looked up.

`tap_region_registrations` scans every element in the tree, and walks each element's ancestor chain via `nearest_tap_surface`, once per tap surface on every primary Down/Up (dispatch_tap_regions line 769). Collect the registrations once per tap event (or cache a per-surface list maintained on mount/unmount/update with a dirty flag), then reuse that list for all surfaces. Confirm the cost with a benchmark before and after.

`TapRegionGroupId::Named(String)` makes `group_id.clone()` a heap allocation for every tap-region element on every primary Down/Up. Make `TapRegistration` borrow from the element instead: `group_id: Option<&'a TapRegionGroupId>` and `callbacks: &'a TapRegionCallbacks` (lines 20-30 and 689-729). The dispatch code only reads them. Use the same change for the TextFieldTapRegion arm at line 716.

`dispatch_tap_regions` allocates on every primary Down/Up: the `surfaces` Vec (757), a `registrations` Vec per surface (769), `hit_groups` HashSet (773), `inside` Vec (778), `inside_ids` HashSet (788) and `outside` Vec (792). Keep these in reusable scratch buffers on `self.input`, or compute `inside` flags into one reused `Vec<bool>` and check group membership by scanning the small `hit_groups` buffer. Using `&TapRegionGroupId` borrows (see the finding for line 707) removes the HashSet hashing of cloned Strings as well.

`raw_gesture_factories` allocates and clones the whole factory slice for each element, and it is called per hit element inside the Down loop at line 862. Avoid the Vec: read each factory's `type_id` by index in the loop (for example `factory_count(element)` plus `factory_type_id(element, index)`), or copy only the `TypeId`s into a reusable `Vec<TypeId>` on `self.input`. Borrow `self.elements` and `self.input.raw_recognizers` as disjoint fields to avoid the conflict that forced the clone.

`raw_gesture_elements` builds a fresh HashSet on every primary Down. Hit lists are short, so dedupe with a reusable `Vec<ElementId>` scratch buffer on `self.input` and `contains`, or `Vec::with_capacity(hit.len())`. Keep the output buffer reusable too, since its result is only iterated in `dispatch_raw_gesture_stream`.

Every Move/Up/Cancel event on an active raw gesture stream allocates `active_members` (line 901) and `dispositions` (line 908, from `GestureArena::entries`, which returns a Vec). Iterate `members` by index without collecting, and replace `disposition_for(&dispositions, member)` with a single-member query such as `self.input.gesture_arena.disposition(key, member)` that does not allocate. Add that query to `incular-gestures` arena.rs next to `entries`.

`self.input.gesture_arena.entries(key)` is called again inside the reject loop (line 950) and inside the accept loop (line 955: `disposition_for(&self.input.gesture_arena.entries(key), member)`), so each rejected or accepted member allocates a fresh Vec. Use the single-member disposition query from the finding for line 901 in the accept check, and call `entries` at most once per reject batch rather than once per member.
